lines.text: Have you ever wondered why there is no bridge between Russia and America?
At its narrowest, the Bering Strait is only 82 kilometres wide.
lines.say: At its narrowest, the Bering Strait is only eighty-two kilometres wide.

lines.text: And in the middle sit two islands: Big Diomede is Russian, Little Diomede is American.
lines.say: And in the middle sit two islands. Big Diomede is Russian. Little Diomede is American.
They are just three point eight kilometres apart.

lines.text: But the International Date Line runs between them, so the Russian island is almost a full day ahead.
cap: is almost a full day ahead

lines.text: Locals call them Yesterday Island and Tomorrow Island.
The water isn't the problem: the strait is only 55 metres deep. The Channel Tunnel runs deeper.
lines.say: The water isn't the problem. The strait is only fifty-five metres deep. The Channel Tunnel runs deeper.

lines.text: The problem is the ice. In winter, floes almost two metres thick grind through it, at nearly minus 50 degrees.
lines.say: The problem is the ice. In winter, floes almost two metres thick grind through it, at nearly minus fifty degrees.

lines.text: And a bridge would connect nothing to nothing: the nearest highway in Alaska is 1,200 kilometres away. In Russia, 2,000.
lines.say: And a bridge would connect nothing to nothing. The nearest highway in Alaska is twelve hundred kilometres away. In Russia, two thousand.

lines.text: Plans have existed since 1890. In 2011, Russia backed a 65-billion-dollar plan.
lines.say: Plans have existed since eighteen ninety. In twenty eleven, Russia backed a sixty-five billion dollar plan.

lines.text: So in 1987, one American simply swam across, from one island to the other, in two hours.
lines.say: So in nineteen eighty-seven, one American simply swam across, from one island to the other, in two hours.
cap: from one island to the other
